newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-BALLESTEROS OUT WITH BAD BACK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BALLESTEROS OUT WITH BAD BACK.

text.p: Seve Ballesteros suffered a blow in his bid to be Europe's Ryder Cup playing captain when he withdrew from the British PGA championship with a bad back on Saturday.
Ballesteros, skipper for the September 26-28 match against the Americans, pulled out before he started his second round.
"He could be struggling for two days or two weeks," said Tour physiotherapist Jonathan Shrewsbury.
Ballesteros, who shot a 76 in the opening round, would have needed at least a six-shot improvement to avoid missing the halfway cut for the seventh time in nine events this year.
When he arrived on Saturday, he went to the physiotherapy caravan to seek treatment for severe pain in his lower back.
"We decided to inject him with a local anaesthetic but it didn't help. He felt it was better to pull out. He couldn't move," Shrewsbury said.
Before making his decision, Ballesteros tried hitting a few pitch shots on the practice range but soon indicated he was in too much pain to play.
"It's nothing new. It's part of the problem. It's not something you can find a miracle cure for," Shrewsbury added.

Ballesteros, currently 29th on the list from which the top 10 will receive an automatic place in the Ryder Cup team, has insisted he hoped to qualify by right. But he might select himself if he does not.
He said this week he felt his game was improving despite his poor start to the year.
He has made the cut in his last two events, finishing 26th and 29th, and is scheduled to play in next week's Tournament Players' Championship of Europe in Germany.
